paper.title: Calculation of Optimum Parameters for Alternating Direction Implicit Procedures (Algorithm 460)
paper.venue: ACM Transactions on Mathematical Software 16(10), p. 633 (Oct 1973), per the frame item and the shipped 460.gz shar header; article text not read

field: numerics (alternating direction implicit iteration, optimal ADI acceleration parameters)
stack: Fortran (netlib CALGO 460.gz, Fortran/Dp/Src/src.f and Fortran/Dp/Drivers/driver.f; gfortran from conda-forge via micromamba in the sandbox)

claim.text: The DMU printed by the shipped driver for ITNS = 1 agrees with the shipped reference output value 0.0775958 within absolute tolerance 1e-7 (registered before any run; the claim is the code's own printed output, not a value read from the paper).
claim.determinism: deterministic (adip is a closed computation on fixed a, b, c, d and n; no random numbers)

attempt: G1: the authors' Fortran compiled with gfortran as shipped (src.f from Fortran/Dp/Src with driver.f from Fortran/Dp/Drivers, one command, binary in a scratch directory; no file edited) and ran as documented. Pass 1 default optimisation, pass 2 -O2 in a clean directory: both print DMU = 0.775958E-01 for ITNS = 1, and the full output matches the shipped res file line for line. The archive's Makefile expects src.f in the driver directory, so it was not used as the build driver; the same compile was run directly on the archive's own files.

original_attempt.reason: not applicable: the shipped source compiled and ran as documented
